wolfram.note: JacobiCN(z,1)'s exact table deliberately returns 1/Cosh(z) rather than the Sech head — see exactSCDN's comment in jacobi-elliptic.ts: sharing Cosh(z) as one denominator avoids a ComplexInfinity/ComplexInfinity collision at Cosh(z)=0 that a Sech-based ratio would hit. Same value as Wolfram's Sech(z), different (deliberately chosen) canonical head.

JacobiCN's numeric kernel is deliberately plain-double (AGM_TOL=1e-15, see jacobi-elliptic.ts's file header) and declines rather than dress up ~17 correct digits as 50 requested ones — matches the 'decline rather than answer wrong' numerics rule. A bignum/arbitrary-precision elliptic kernel is a real feature, out of scope here.
